esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the cervical spine during scapular retraction and flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees flexed and the feet supported. Maintain the gaze toward the ceiling. Translate the chin posteriorly without flexing or extending the cervical spine. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain an upright thoracic posture, keep the shoulders relaxed, and perform the cervical movement slowly and precisely.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the cervical spine during flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Lie supine with the knees flexed and the feet supported. Perform a gentle cervical retraction, then lift the head approximately 2 to 3 cm while maintaining the retracted position. Hold for 3 to 5 seconds, then lower the head slowly.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain an upright thoracic posture, keep the shoulders relaxed, and perform the cervical movement slowly and precisely.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Isometric Cervical Flexion with Manual Resistance
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the cervical spine, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand. Place one palm against the forehead. Apply gentle forward pressure with the head while the hand provides equal resistance so that no visible movement occurs. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Isometric Cervical Flexion with Manual Resistance

esercizi.nome: Seated Cervical Extension with Controlled Jaw Opening
esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the cervical spine during extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair. Start by looking straight ahead. Slowly tilt your head upward toward the ceiling. Once comfortable, gently open your mouth, then close it again while keeping your head tilted up. Return your head to the starting position slowly. Repeat 5 times.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain an upright thoracic posture, keep the shoulders relaxed, and perform the cervical movement slowly and precisely.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Seated Cervical Extension with Controlled Jaw Opening

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the cervical spine, with emphasis on lateral flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair with your arms relaxed by your sides. Slowly bring your right ear toward your right shoulder, without lifting your shoulder. Stop when you feel a gentle stretch on the left side. Hold for 5 seconds, return to the centre, then repeat the same movement to the left.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Isometric Cervical Lateral Flexion with Manual Resistance
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the cervical spine, with emphasis on lateral flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright or stand. Place one palm against the temporal region above the ear. Apply gentle lateral pressure with the head while the hand provides equal resistance so that no visible movement occurs. Hold for 5 seconds, then repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Isometric Cervical Lateral Flexion with Manual Resistance

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve active range of motion and movement control of the cervical spine during rotation.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the shoulders relaxed. Rotate the head slowly to one side through the available comfortable range. Hold for 3 to 5 seconds, return to neutral, and repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain an upright thoracic posture, keep the shoulders relaxed, and perform the cervical movement slowly and precisely.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the cervical spine, with emphasis on lateral flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair. Bring your right ear toward your right shoulder. Gently place your right hand on top of your head, near your left ear. Use only the weight of your hand to guide the movement downward, without pulling forcefully. Hold for 5 seconds, then repeat on the opposite side.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the cervical spine, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with both hands resting on the thighs. Flex the cervical spine slowly by directing the chin toward the sternum. Hold a mild posterior cervical stretch for 5 seconds, then return to neutral.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.

esercizi.nome: Isometric Cervical Extension with Manual Resistance
esercizi.description: This exercise uses a submaximal isometric contraction to develop neuromuscular control of the cervical spine, with emphasis on extension.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright and place both hands against the occipital region. Apply gentle posterior pressure with the head while the hands provide equal resistance so that no visible movement occurs. Hold for 5 seconds, then relax.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain neutral joint alignment, apply a steady submaximal contraction, and continue breathing throughout the hold.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.
esercizi.imageAlt: Isometric Cervical Extension with Manual Resistance

esercizi.description: This mobility exercise provides a controlled stretch to the cervical spine, with emphasis on flexion.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright on a chair. Interlace your hands and place them gently behind your head. Let your head drop forward toward your chest, using only the weight of your arms to guide the movement downward. You should not pull forcefully. Hold for 5 seconds, then slowly return to the starting position.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain stable alignment and progress gradually to a mild, tolerable stretch while breathing normally.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.

esercizi.description: This exercise is intended to improve motor control and stability of the cervical spine during scapular retraction.
esercizi.howToDo: Sit upright with the elbows flexed and the hands near the shoulders. Move the elbows posteriorly while gently retracting the scapulae. Hold for 5 seconds, then return to neutral.
esercizi.whatToDo: Maintain an upright thoracic posture, keep the shoulders relaxed, and perform the cervical movement slowly and precisely.
esercizi.whatNotToDo: Do not force cervical end range or use momentum. Stop if dizziness, radiating symptoms, numbness, or sharp pain occurs.
